  San Gabriel, California 91776

   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, January 7, 2020

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Menchaca
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Pu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Costanzo,
  Harrington, Liao

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF MICHAEL CAMMARANO
  B. STATE OF NEIGHBORHOOD IMPROVEMENT SERVICES
  C. CENSUS UPDATE 2020

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council
  on items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes.
  You will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  2
   The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of December 3, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – NOVEMBER 2019

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of November 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-01 AMENDING THE CITY’S 2019-20
  CITYWIDE FEE SCHEDULE

  The 2019-20 Citywide Fee Schedule, represents the fees charged by the City
  for various licenses, permits, facility rentals, and services provided to
  residents, developers, program users and the general public, was adopted on
  September 17, 2019 by Resolution No. 19-31. Since its adoption, staff has
  continued to review the schedule and has proposed various changes. The
  adoption of the proposed resolution will amend the 2019-20 Citywide Fee
  Schedule rather than replace it. Once approved the Citywide Fee Schedule will
  be updated and refreshed on the City’s website.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-01 adopting the
  recommended fees and further amending the 2019-20 City’s Citywide Fee
  Schedule to reflect these changes. The new fees will become effective
  immediately upon passage of the resolution.

  E. FIRST AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND MARK LAZZARETTO

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  3
   The proposed First Amendment to the City Manager Employment Agreement
  would extend the City Manager’s term of employment by an additional two
  (2) years. No change in salary, benefits, or other provision of any kind is
  proposed to the City Manager Employment Agreement. The City Council
  recently completed its second evaluation of the City Manager’s performance
  and determined that, based on a positive performance review, to extend the
  term of the Agreement for an additional two (2) years.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the First Amendment to the
  City Manager Employment Agreement between the City of San Gabriel and
  Mark Lazzaretto.

  F. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 660
  AMENDING TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE – FINANCE AND REVENUE

  The proposed Ordinance No. 660 will amend Title III, Section 34 of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code by providing additional definitions, budget
  administration procedures, and annual audit requirements. The first reading
  of this proposed ordinance was conducted on December 3, 2019.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading, read by title only,
  and adopt at the 2nd reading, Ordinance No. 660 amending Title III, Section
  34 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, pertaining to Budget Administration
  and Annual Audit.

  G. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY SAN GABRIEL SEA
  GULLS

  The San Gabriel Sea Gulls (SGSG) and Gabrielino High School use Smith Park
  Pool for their swim team use. Both teams contribute to the cost of the pool
  operation during the school year. SGSG also covers a portion of the pool cost
  for their use of the pool during the summer months. As part of the Fiscal Year
  2019-2020 Budget, the fee for SGSG pool use was set at $57.64 per hour,
  which includes the hourly cost of one Lifeguard, and a portion of utilities and
  maintenance of the pool. With the potential rate increase of staff and change
  in rates for utilities, this hourly fee may change for fiscal year 2020-2021. As
  such, this agreement is proposed to end on June 30, 2020.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends approval of the attached agreement for San Gabriel Sea
  Gulls use of Smith Park Pool to be effective immediately and ending June 30,
  2020.

  H. THEATER RENTAL FEE WAIVER  REQUEST:  AMERICAN  CHINESE
  CULTURAL ASSOCIATION

  The American Chinese Culture Association (ACCA) has approached the City of
  San Gabriel with a request for waiver of the theater rental fee for their
  upcoming free performance on January 26, 2020. ACCA is planning a free
  performance to be held at the Mission Playhouse to promote Asian arts and
  culture through a variety of performing arts. There will be no tickets sold and
  no entrance fee collected, which will allow access to all who are interested.
  The event will be open to the general public from San Gabriel and
  surrounding areas. The American Chinese Culture Association (ACCA)
  requests to waive the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse rental fee of $4,220.00
  for the upcoming community performance.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approves American Chinese Cultural
  Association request to waive the theater rental fee of $4,220.00 for the
  rehearsal and performance of the upcoming free admission community
  performance on January 26, 2020.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT RELATING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF
  ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING
  UNITS (ZTA19-003)

  In October 2019, Governor Newsom signed multiple bills (Senate Bill 13,
  Assembly Bill 68, and Assembly Bill 881) which would amend the existing State
  law pertaining to Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs). The new bills would take
  effect on January 1, 2020. An ADU ordinance that is not in full compliance
  with the amended State law would become invalid. The City is now tasked
  with amending the ADU regulations in order to ensure compliance with State
  law while preserving the character of single- and multi-family neighborhoods
  to the greatest extent feasible.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  5
   On December 16, 2019, the Planning Commission held a special meeting to
  consider the proposed Zone Text Amendment (ZTA) related to the
  development of ADUs and Junior ADUs. The Planning Commission
  recommended the approval of planning case number ZTA19-003 with a vote
  of 4-0, with the condition that the Planning Division staff consult with the City
  Attorney to address the items brought forward from the public
  correspondence.

  Recommended Action:

  The City Council is requested to:

  1. ADOPT Ordinance No. 661 amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning Code)
  in order to amend the zoning definitions and development standards to
  allow accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units in all
  zones that allow single or multi-family units on-site, consistent with the
  applicable State law. Staff is recommending that the City Council adopt
  the Urgency Ordinance in order for the Ordinance to take effect
  immediately.

  2. INTRODUCE for first reading by title only Ordinance No. 662 of the City
  Council of the City of San Gabriel, California; waive further reading of
  Ordinance No. 662; and Schedule the second reading and adoption of
  Ordinance No. 662 for January 21, 2020.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ACCEPTANCE OF ANNUAL AUDIT REPORTS, FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE
  30, 2019

  The certified public accounting firm of White Nelson Diehl Evans LLP (WNDE)
  was engaged by the City Council to perform an audit of the financial
  statements and perform compliance testing of the City of San Gabriel for the
  fiscal year ended June 30, 2019. WNDE conducted the audit in accordance
  with generally accepted auditing standards and issued an unmodified (clean)
  audit opinion on the financial statements. This report provides brief summary
  of the audit report to be used as a companion to the published
  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the annual audit
  reports for fiscal year ended June 30, 2019.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  6
   B. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-03, APPROVING THE
  APPOINTMENT OF KENNETH L. LOUIE TO INTERIM FINANCE DIRECTOR,
  AND RESOLUTION NO. 20-04, UPDATING THE AUTHORIZED LIST OF
  DESIGNATED CITY OFFICIALS TO OPEN, MAINTAIN AND MAKE
  TRANSACTIONS IN CITY ACCOUNTS IN VARIOUS BANKS AND
  FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

  The adoption of Resolution No. 20-03 will approve an employment
  agreement with retired CalPERS annuitant Kenneth L. Louie for Interim
  Finance Director, and Resolution No. 20-04, which removes outgoing Acting
  Finance Director Paula Chamberlain and adds incoming Interim Finance
  Director Kenneth L. Louie to the list of signature authorities on the City’s
  various treasury/financial accounts. The term of the employment agreement
  shall be limited to 960 hours per fiscal year, with a final expiration date of
  December 31, 2020. If approved, both actions shall be effective on January 8,
  2020. Mr. Louie will oversee the FY 2020-21 budget, manage the day-to-day
  operations of the Finance Department, continue with the review and revision
  of the City’s fiscal policies, continue current projects, and assist with the City’s
  on-going recruitment for a permanent Finance Director.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-03,
  approving an employment agreement between Kenneth L. Louie and the City
  of San Gabriel for Interim Finance Director, and Resolution No. 20-04,
  removing outgoing Acting Finance Director Paula Chamberlain and adding
  incoming Finance Director Kenneth L. Louie to the list of signature authorities
  on the City’s various treasury/financial accounts.

  C. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-05 AUTHORIZING THE
  AMENDMENT OF THE SALARY SCHEDULE TO COMPLY WITH
  CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE REQUIREMENTS EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1,
  2020

  Effective January 1, 2020, the California minimum wage increased to $13.00
  per hour. To ensure the City is compliant with State law, staff is recommending
  salary range increases of those classification impacted by the new minimum
  wage by adoption of Resolution No. 20-05. There are 13 part-time position
  classifications that will be impacted by the new minimum wage. There are
  approximately 89 employees in the positions effected by the resolution. The
  cost of the increase will be absorbed within department budget and reviewed
  with the Mid-Year Budget Review.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  7
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-05
  increasing salary ranges effective January 1, 2020, for those classifications
  impacted by the increase in the California Minimum Wage law and approving
  the Salary Schedule as presented.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 6.  CLOSED SESSION – None.

 7.  ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, January 21, 2020
  at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
  Gabriel, California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 7, 2020  8

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT RELATING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UN ITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (ZTA19 -003)

  Presentation was made by Assistant Planner Anthony Alvarado.

  Mayor Pu opened the public hearing.

  Isela Bowles, resident, requested that additional wording be added to the zone
  amendment to clarify that an addition of an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) does

I  not supersede requirements for parking.

  There was no one else wishing to speak; therefore, Mayor Pu closed the public
  hearing.

  Council discussion included how the new regulations would affect applications in
  progress and multi-family units; how square-footage requirements are calculated;
  new owner-occupancy provisions; garage conversion to ADU; ADU regulations
  controlling on R- 1 improvements; the need to re-visit parking regulations citywide;
  how ADU floor area ratio (FAR) is calculated; reassessment; Junior ADUs are subject

   to Building Code requirements for the single-family home they are contained in;
  and fees and process for amendments to existing applications and site-reviews.
  City Manager Lazzaretto commented that staff is preparing an amendment on
  parking regulations for City Council consideration in February or March 2020.

  A motion was made by Council Member Liao, seconded by Council Member

  standards to allow accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units in

  City Manager Lazzaretto commented that he has not yet heard back regard ing th e

  Assistant City Manager/Community Development Director Chaparyan added that a

  City Manager Lazzaretto thanked the City Council for the extension of his contract,

I  stated that he has enjoyed working with the Council and the community, and

I  Vice Mayor Menchaca wished everyone a Happy New Decade, commended front desk
